n: In this section we become acquainted with the neuroleptic substances: aminazine, diprazine, tizercin, haloperidol and droperidol. We shall consider methods of isolating them from physical evidence and of analysing them. Key terms: phenothiazine, neuroleptic, the Salomatin method, FPN reagent, TLC, Rf st, UV spectrophotometry and IR spectrometry. The outline is as follows: classification, isolation, preliminary examination of urine, TLC, individual substances and butyrophenones.

The history of phenothiazine. Phenothiazine, that is thiodiphenylamine, was first used in medicine as an anthelmintic and antiseptic drug, and later to treat inflammation of the urinary tract. Because highly active drugs of low toxicity have been synthesised, phenothiazine itself is no longer used in medicine. By 1945 the hydrogen attached to the nucleus nitrogen had been replaced by alkylaminoalkyl radicals, giving highly active compounds. Many of them are neuroleptics.

Classification of phenothiazine derivatives. By chemical structure, phenothiazine derivatives are divided into three groups. The aliphatic group includes aminazine, propazine and levomepromazine. The piperazine group includes meteperazine, etaperazine, triftazine and fluphenazine. The representatives of the piperidine group are thioridazine and periciazine.

t: Characteristics and significance of the groups
n: Characteristics of the groups. Besides its antipsychotic action, the first group has a calming effect: it produces weakness, passivity, and apathetic and hypnosedative states. The second group, besides its main antipsychotic action, shows a stimulating effect and produces active hyperkinetic and dyskinetic states. The third group has weaker antipsychotic activity and has no hypnosedative effect. Some of them potentiate the action of narcotic and intoxicating substances, and therefore have toxicological and narcological significance.

The first stage of isolation by the Salomatin method. The specimen is steeped with a 10% alcoholic solution of oxalic acid for 2 hours, and this is repeated 3 times. The alcoholic extracts are combined and evaporated on a water bath at 40°C to a syrupy consistency. Foreign substances are precipitated with 96% ethyl alcohol. The alcoholic extracts are evaporated to a dry residue.

The second part of the isolation. The residue is dissolved in hot water, acidified with a 5% solution of oxalic acid to pH=2-3 and extracted with diethyl ether. The ether layer is used for detecting barbiturates or is discarded. The medium of the aqueous solution is brought to pH=13 with a 50% solution of sodium hydroxide and extracted three times with diethyl ether. From the ether extract, the phenothiazine derivatives are re-extracted with 0.5 M sulphuric acid in portions of 10, 10, 10 and 5 ml, and analysed.

Preliminary examination of urine. In the first method, 1 ml of a mixture of 60 ml of 10% H2SO4 and 20 ml of 5% FeCl3 is added to 1 ml of urine; a dark red-pink colour results. In the second method, 1 ml of a mixture of 5 ml of 5% FeCl3, 45 ml of 20% HClO4 and 50 ml of 50% HNO3 is added to 1 ml of urine; a light red-pink colour appears. The FPN reagent consists of iron(III) chloride, perchloric acid and nitric acid in the ratio 5:45:50.

Evaluating the result of the preliminary examination. If no colour develops in the reactions, it may be concluded that phenothiazine derivatives are absent. If the reactions are positive, to confirm the presence of phenothiazines they are isolated from blood and urine by liquid-liquid extraction and identified by other methods. Remember: salicylates and other co-extracted substances interfere with the detection.

Isolation from blood and urine. 10 ml of urine and 2 ml of blood, in separate vessels, are brought to pH=13 with 50% NaOH and heated; this is done for 10 minutes in a bath at 100°C. The hydrolysate is extracted twice, with 20 ml portions of n-heptane containing 3% isoamyl alcohol, and washed with water. The extract is divided into two equal parts: one for TLC, the other for identity and quantity.

Sample preparation for TLC. A part of the extract is evaporated to dryness in a stream of hot air. The residue is dissolved in 0.2-0.5 ml of chloroform. The solution is applied with a capillary tube to the starting line of 2 TLC plates. In the same row as the sample under test, a standard sample of aminazine or a solution of the suspected phenothiazine derivative is always spotted as a marker.

Chromatographic systems for TLC. The first system consists of benzene, dioxane and 25% ammonia in the ratio 60:35:5. The second system consists of ethyl acetate, acetone and NH3-ethanol in the ratio 50:45:4. As the visualising agent, a 1:9 mixture of H2SO4 and ethanol is sprayed on, or Marquis reagent is applied.

The Rf st values are given relative to aminazine, that is, for aminazine it equals 1. The table gives two values for each substance: in the first and the second system. For diprazine, 0.74 and 2.9, the spot is dark red. For deniazine, 2.1 and 2.9, the spot is red. For propazine, 1.3 and 1.08, the spot is red. The colour of the spots is assessed with the 1:9 mixture of sulphuric acid and ethanol and with Marquis reagent.

Rf st values, continued. For levomepromazine, 1.56 and 1.87, the spot is blue. For mepazine, 1.47 and 1.60, the spot is red. For triftazine, 0.48 and 0.26, the spot is red. For etaperazine, 0.34 and 0.48, the spot is dark red. For phrenolone, the Rf st is 1.71 in the first system and 3.21 in the second, the spot is red. So the levomepromazine spot is blue, and the others are red or dark red.

Evaluating TLC results and purification. Besides the Rf st, attention is also paid to the formation of other spots. If there is an additional spot, the second part of the heptane aliquot must be purified by TLC. The spot zone is located only by applying the reagent to the marker zone. For purification, the strip is chromatographed with the marker, the sorbent is scraped off with a scalpel and eluted with a 1:1 mixture of ethanol and ammonia, then filtered and evaporated.

Structure and properties of aminazine. Aminazine is 2-chloro-10-(3-dimethylaminopropyl)-phenothiazine hydrochloride. Its synonyms are chlorpromazine, chlorazine, largactil and plegomazine. It is a white or faintly pinkish fine crystalline powder; it is very hygroscopic and darkens under sunlight. It dissolves well in water, ethyl alcohol and chloroform, and is practically insoluble in diethyl ether. Its aqueous solution is acidic; in an alkaline medium it dissolves well in organic solvents.

The narcological significance of aminazine. Aminazine is the main representative of substances with neuroleptic action; despite the development of new neuroleptics, it continues to be used in medicine. It has a strong sedative effect on the central nervous system and relaxes skeletal muscles, while consciousness remains preserved. It potentiates the action of hypnotics, barbiturates, narcotics, analgesics, local anaesthetics and psychotropic substances.

Use and dose of aminazine. The drug has a strong antiemetic effect and, owing to its hypothermic action, is used for artificial cooling of the body. It is used in insomnia, pruritic dermatoses, psychoses and neuroses; it reduces vascular permeability. Treatment may last from 3-4 weeks to 3-4 months or more. The daily dose ranges from 0.075 g to 0.6 g. At the end of treatment the dose of the drug should be reduced gradually.

Metabolism of aminazine. Aminazine is metabolised in a complex way by sulphoxidation, demethylation, N-oxidation and hydroxylation. The literature indicates that more than 20 of its metabolites have been identified. The main metabolites are excreted in the urine; some form conjugates with sulphuric and glucuronic acids. A small part is excreted unchanged in the urine, so aminazine can be identified in it directly.

Colour reactions of aminazine. With concentrated H2SO4 it gives a crimson-red colour. With concentrated HNO3 it gives red-pink, and with concentrated HCl first pink and then red. With Marquis reagent a green colour appears first, then red-pink. With Mandelin reagent it gives green first and, on standing, red. With Dragendorff reagent an amorphous precipitate forms first, then quadrangular brown crystals.

t: Aminazine: TLC, UV, IR and quantification
n: Aminazine: TLC, UV, IR and quantification. For TLC, a mixture of benzene, dioxane and 25% ammonia in the ratio 70:20:5 is taken; the visualising agent is Marquis reagent or H2SO4-ethanol 1:9; a pink-violet colour forms at Rf=0.93. In the UV spectrum, a solution in 0.1 M sulphuric acid absorbs at 255 and 307 nm; the main metabolite, the sulphoxide, gives maxima at 239, 274, 300 and 341 nm. In the IR spectrum, in a potassium bromide disc, absorption is observed in the regions of 1561, 1455, 1402, 1240 and 747 cm-1. The quantity is determined from the UV spectrum or from the absorbance of the red colour formed with concentrated H2SO4, that is, by photoelectric colorimetry (PEC).

Propazine. Propazine is 10-(3-dimethylaminopropyl)-phenothiazine hydrochloride. Its pharmacological action is sedative, similar to aminazine; it reduces motor activity and has antiemetic and hypothermic effects. It potentiates the action of hypnotics, barbiturates, narcotic and local analgesic substances. It is less toxic than aminazine and is used together with many neuroleptic drugs.

Detecting propazine in extracts. In rapid analysis of urine, the FPN reagent is used; it consists of iron(III) chloride, perchloric acid and nitric acid in the ratio 5:45:50. With this reagent propazine gives a pink-violet colour. For TLC, a mixture of benzene, dioxane and 25% ammonia in the ratio 70:20:5 is taken, with Marquis reagent or H2SO4-ethanol 1:9 as the visualising agent; a pink-violet colour forms at Rf=0.71. The quantity is determined by PEC on the basis of the colour produced with the FPN reagent, or by the UV spectrophotometric method.

Diprazine. Diprazine, that is pipolphen, promethazine, protazine, is a white crystalline powder. It dissolves well in water at 1:60, in ethyl alcohol at 1:9 and in chloroform at 1:2, and is practically insoluble in ether. The drug is extracted by organic solvents in an alkaline medium. It has antihistamine activity with a sedative effect; it potentiates the action of narcotic, hypnotic, neuroleptic and analgesic substances. It is used in allergic diseases, pruritic dermatoses and in the treatment of encephalitis.

Metabolism and colour reactions of diprazine. Diprazine sulphoxide is detectable in urine even after 14 days. Unconjugated diprazine is also excreted in the urine. With concentrated H2SO4 it gives a crimson-red colour. With concentrated HNO3 it gives light red, crimson-red and yellow; with concentrated HCl a reddish pink, crimson-pink colour appears. With Marquis reagent a crimson colour forms. With Mandelin reagent it gives green first, then crimson; the Vitali-Morin reaction is also used.

t: Diprazine: TLC, UV and IR methods
n: Determination of diprazine by TLC, UV and IR. The TLC conditions are the same as for aminazine; diprazine gives Rf=0.72. In the UV spectrum, maxima are observed at 252 and 301 nm in a 1:1 mixture of water and ethyl alcohol, and at 249 and 300 nm in 0.1 M sulphuric acid. In the IR spectrum, in a potassium bromide disc, there is absorption in the regions of 1459, 1222 and 757 cm-1. The quantity is determined from the UV spectrum by spectrophotometry or photoelectric colorimetry.

Etaperazine. Etaperazine is a piperazine derivative and a considerably more potent neuroleptic than aminazine. It relaxes muscles, has antiemetic and anti-hiccup action, and potentiates the action of sleeping drugs. In TLC under the aminazine conditions, Rf=0.32; in the UV spectrum, 252 and 301 nm in a 1:1 water-ethanol mixture. In colour reactions, a dark red colour forms with concentrated H2SO4, and light red and then dark red with concentrated HNO3. With Marquis reagent it gives a dark red colour.

Periciazine and distinguishing the phenothiazines. Periciazine is 2-cyano-10-[3-(4-hydroxypiperidino)-propyl]-phenothiazine; it has weak antipsychotic activity. It potentiates the action of hypnotics, barbiturates, narcotic substances and analgesics. Propazine, etaperazine and periciazine, like other phenothiazine derivatives, are metabolised in a complex way; the isolation methods are the same. To distinguish these substances, thin-layer, gas-liquid and high-performance liquid chromatography and spectral methods of analysis are chiefly used.

Tizercin. Tizercin, that is levomepromazine, levopromazine, methotrimeprazine, is a white crystalline powder. It dissolves well in ethyl alcohol, diethyl ether and chloroform, and poorly in water; in an alkaline medium it dissolves well in organic solvents. It has adrenolytic, antihistamine and analgesic action; it has a rapid and strong sedative effect. It is used as a calming agent in psychoses, alcoholic psychosis, insomnia and dermatoses.

Metabolism and isolation of tizercin. Tizercin is metabolised by oxidation, hydroxylation, sulphoxidation and N-demethylation; it also forms conjugates with sulphuric and glucuronic acids. About 10% is excreted in the urine unchanged, as the sulphoxide or as the glucuronide. Tizercin is isolated from biological material in the same way as aminazine.

Reactions for detecting tizercin. With Marquis reagent it gives a bluish red colour, and with Fröhde reagent a reddish blue. If, after Mandelin reagent is added, the mixture is cooled and concentrated sulphuric acid is then added, a red-pink colour appears. In TLC, a 1:1 mixture of 25% ammonia and ethanol, ethyl acetate and acetone are used; the visualising agent is a 50% solution of H2SO4 in alcohol, at 100°C for 3-5 minutes, giving a red spot.

t: Tizercin: UV, IR and quantitative analysis
n: Tizercin: UV, IR and quantitative analysis. In the UV spectrum, a solution in ethyl alcohol gives maxima at 255 and 310 nm, and a solution in 0.1 M hydrochloric acid at 251 and 302 nm. In the IR spectrum, a potassium bromide disc absorbs in the regions of 1587, 1460, 1269 and 1446 cm-1. The quantity is determined from the UV spectrum by spectrophotometry or photoelectric colorimetry.

Properties of haloperidol and droperidol. Haloperidol is a white to yellowish amorphous or crystalline powder; it is practically insoluble in water and dissolves in methanol at 1:55. Droperidol is a white amorphous or crystalline powder; it darkens in light and is practically insoluble in water. The solubility ratios are: in ethanol, haloperidol 1:50 and droperidol 1:140; in chloroform, 1:20 and 1:40; in diethyl ether, 1:200 and 1:500.

Action of haloperidol and droperidol. Haloperidol is a strong neuroleptic; it has sedative and antiemetic effects, reduces aggression, and potentiates the action of other psychotropic substances. An overdose is accompanied by disturbance of motor activity and ends in death in 15-22% of cases; the main metabolite is 4-(4-chlorophenyl)-4-hydroxypiperidine. Droperidol is a rapid, strong, short-acting neuroleptic: it acts within 3-10 minutes, and the duration of action is 3-24 hours. It is metabolised mainly in the liver, and 10% is excreted unchanged by the kidneys. It is used in anaesthesia, before preparation for narcosis.

t: Isolating butyrophenones from blood and urine
n: Isolating butyrophenones from blood and urine. 10 ml of urine and 2 ml of blood are brought to pH=13 with 50% NaOH and heated for 30 minutes in a boiling bath. The cooled hydrolysate is extracted three times with ethyl acetate. The extracts are filtered through anhydrous Na2SO4 and evaporated. The residue is dissolved in 95% alcohol and subjected to TLC.

Identifying haloperidol and droperidol. In TLC, the systems toluene-acetone-ammonia 50:10:5, toluene-hexane-acetone-diethylamine 10:30:5:5, ethanol-ammonia 100:1.5, toluene-hexane-diethylamine 10:40:10 and others are used. To locate the spots on the plate, irradiation with UV at 254 nm and Dragendorff reagent are used. In the UV spectrum, a solution of haloperidol in 95% ethyl alcohol absorbs maximally at 246 nm, and a solution of droperidol in formic acid at 247 and 276 nm.

Colour reactions of butyrophenones. With Marquis reagent, both haloperidol and droperidol form a yellow product. With Fröhde reagent, haloperidol gives an orange colour and droperidol a yellow one. With Mandelin reagent, haloperidol forms a dark orange colour and droperidol a yellow-green one. With the help of these colours the two substances are distinguished from each other.

Quantitative determination of butyrophenones. To a solution of droperidol in hydrochloric acid, 12 ml of acetate buffer, pH=3.5, 2 ml of saturated methyl orange solution and 5 ml of chloroform are added and shaken. The chloroform layer is separated in a separating funnel, and its absorbance is determined photocolorimetrically at 400 nm in a cuvette with a path length of 10 mm. The linear range of the determination is 1-10 µg/ml; the quantity is found from a previously prepared calibration graph. As a more sensitive method, gas chromatography-mass spectrometric analysis may also be used.

Conclusion. Phenothiazines are divided into three groups and are isolated by the Salomatin method: the acid ether layer is for barbiturates, and the alkaline layer, that is pH=13, is for phenothiazines. If the preliminary colour reactions in urine are positive, they are isolated from blood and urine and confirmed by TLC, that is by Rf st and the coloured spots, and by other methods. Aminazine, diprazine and tizercin are identified with acids, Marquis and Mandelin reagents, and UV and IR spectra; butyrophenones give yellow to orange colours. Review questions: name the phenothiazine derivatives, state their toxicological significance, and explain the isolation method, the colour reactions and the preliminary examination of urine.
